battle.name: 徐圓朗起義
battle.brief: 隋大業十三年（617年）正月，魯郡人徐圓朗在兗州聚眾起事，先取金鄉、濟州，後依李密與竇建德；武德二年（619年）降唐，封魯郡公、拜兗州總管，旋於武德四年（621年）八月扣唐使盛彥師反唐，與劉黑闔相呼應攻宋城，終為唐軍所平。卡面這件埃及月牙劍屬青銅時代工藝，比本役早三千餘年，並非此戰場所用；隋唐兩軍所用者為環首橢刀、方天畫戟、長柄槊與蹶張弩，攻城賴撞車、雲梯與石砲。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場戰爭是隋朝末年魯郡（今山東濟寧一帶）的地方起義，與隋、唐以及竇建德、李密、劉黑闔等北方群雄在山東及淮濟地區的拉鋸，時間自隋大業十三年（617年）正月起，到唐武德六年（623年）正月收束，前後六年。徐圓朗一方起初純粹是民間起義眾：以魯郡兗州城為據，自行聚集鄉里，沒有常備建制，也沒有正式的將號體系；起義眾多為魯郡及鄰郡的農戶、獵戶、鹽丁與逃戶，武器多為自備的竹木矛、標槊、弓矢、附帶少量繳自隋軍的環首刀與皮甲，人數在起義初期即達數萬量級（《資治通鑑》只概記「眾數萬」，並無確數，歷代史家多以為其中有誇大）。武德二年（619年）徐圓朗歸唐之後，其部眾被編為兗州總管府下的州兵與縣兵，由唐廷任命的地方官與總管節制，卻仍保留原有的部曲與鄉里編組——這是「起義軍」向「州兵」轉換的節點，也是日後能夠再度反唐的伏線。武德四年（621年）八月反唐之後，其眾在魯郡、杞州、陳州、宋城之間流竄作戰，編制仍以舊部曲為主，號令不齊，攻城靠四面並進的群眾式圍逼，既無攻城器械，也無統一指揮。唐方則是李唐的正規軍：秦王李世民、齊王李元吉、淮安王李神通、行軍總管任瑰、李世勣、史萬寶、王要漢等各領一軍，兵源有關中精騎與河南、山東各州縣募兵，裝備制式齊整，配有弩、槊、攻城車具與輜重；唐廷以行台民部尚書一類職銜統籌河南軍務，汴州總管王要漢與行台民部尚書史萬寶各領一路，可見此役唐方的指揮體系是「中央行台統籌、諸道分進」的格局。第三方之中，竇建德盤據河北的夏國、經營瓦崗的李密、在河北再舉的劉黑闔與淮南的杜伏威，都是隨時可能改變局面的變數；徐圓朗正是靠在其中兩者之間周旋，把山東這一折衝地帶變成各方角力的場所。
countriesEn: This conflict was a local rising in Lu commandery (present-day Jining, Shandong) that turned into a six-year tug of war between the Sui, the Tang, and the northern contenders Dou Jiande, Li Mi and Liu Heitao across the Lu-Si region and the Huai-Ji corridor. It began in the first month of the thirteenth year of Daye (617) and was only closed out in the first month of the sixth year of Wude (623). The Xu Yuanlang side began as a purely popular rising: there was no standing army and no formal system of titles and ranks, and the crowd was drawn from the farming households, hunters, salt workers and runaways of Lu commandery and the neighbouring prefectures. Their weapons were largely self-provided bamboo and wooden spears, throwing pikes, bows and arrows, with a few sabres and leather armours taken from Sui troops; the initial strength is recorded only as several tens of thousands, an approximate figure without any exact count, and most later historians regard it as exaggerated. After Xu surrendered to the Tang in the second year of Wude (619), his men were enrolled as prefectural and county troops under the Yanzhou jiangjun fu and placed under Tang-appointed officials, while still keeping their old bands and village organisation - that was the point at which a rebel army became a prefectural army, and also the reason a fresh rebellion remained possible later. After the revolt of the eighth month of the fourth year of Wude (621), his forces moved about between Lu, Qi, Chen and Song city, still organised around the old bands, with orders that did not match, besieging towns by mass assault from several sides, with neither siege equipment nor unified command. The Tang side fielded a regular army: Prince of Qin Li Shimin, Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, xingjun zongguan Ren Gui, Li Shiji, Shi Wanbao and Wang Yaohan each led a column, with troops from the elite cavalry of Guanzhong together with militia raised in Henan, Shandong and neighbouring prefectures, equipped to standard with crossbows, long pikes, siege wagons and baggage trains. The Tang command structure here was a central xingtai coordinating several separate columns, with the Liangzhou zongguan Wang Yaohan and the xingtai minbu shangshu Shi Wanbao each taking one line, which shows the pattern of a central directorate coordinating and several columns advancing separately. Among third parties abounded Dou Jiande's state of Xia in Hebei, Li Mi's Wagang force, Liu Heitao's renewed rising in Hebei and Du Fuyei in Huainan, all of whom could change the situation at any time; Xu Yuanlang exploited exactly this by moving between two of them and turning this stretch of Shandong into a place where everyone competed.
people: 徐圓朗（？—623年3月26日），隋末魯郡人，是這場起義唯一的核心人物。他並非隋室的將領，家世也不顯赫，靠的是在鄉里之間聚眾起事；起義之後自建號令，先後依附瓦崗寨的李密，李密敗亡則歸於竇建德，武德二年（619年）再降唐，被封為魯郡公、拜兗州總管。這段「先反後降、降而復反」的三段式經歷，決定了徐圓朗既非純粹的起義首領，也非唐廷編制之內的常將。他不是靠正面爭鋒取勝的人：《資治通鑑》記劉黑闔敗後，河間人劉復禮勸他迎劉世徹、奉以帝號，他先則然之，隨即奪其兵、以為司馬，待劉世徹受命徇譙、杞二州、所向皆下、聲勢已起時，又將其殺害，可見其起事所憑是算計與權謀，而不是名分。部將與內應是另一批關鍵人物：濟州別駕劉伯通執刺史竇務本、以濟州歸徐圓朗，是山東最早的一場內應；金鄉人陽孝誠反出徐圓朗、以金鄉城降唐，成為唐軍打開的第一個缺口；杞州守將周文舉在城破被擒；盛彥師是唐廷派往河南安集軍民的使臣，卻在武德四年（621年）八月被徐圓朗扣留，成為反唐的藉口。唐方將領之中，秦王李世民是本役的決定性人物：武德四年秋七月他擊徐圓朗、下十餘城，聲震淮泗，迫使淮南杜伏威入朝；行台民部尚書史萬寶拔陳州，汴州總管王要漢拔杞州，淮安王李神通、行軍總管任瑰、李世勣則在秦王掃平淮濟之後接續進攻，最終迫徐圓朗出城。劉黑闔、李密、竇建德、杜伏威四位割據者，是決定徐圓朗命運的外部人物：劉黑闔一敗，徐圓朗即驚惶失措；竇建德曾收容他，李密則是他一度依附的對象；而竇務本、陽孝誠、周文舉、劉復禮、劉世徹這些州吏、城守與謀士，則是使局面屢次翻轉的關節。
peopleEn: Xu Yuanlang (?-26 March 623) was a native of Lu commandery in the last years of the Sui and the single central figure of this rising. He was not a general of the Sui court and came from no distinguished family; what he had was the ability to gather a crowd in his own home district. After the rising he set up his own orders and names, attached himself first to Li Mi of the Wagang stronghold, went over to Dou Jiande when Li Mi fell, and in the second year of Wude (619) surrendered to the Tang, receiving the title of Duke of Lu and the office of jiangjun of Yanzhou. That three-stage career of revolt, submission and renewed revolt settled his position: he was neither a pure rebel leader nor a regular general inside the Tang establishment. He was not a man who won by frontal fighting. When Liu Heitao was defeated, Liu Fuli of Hejian urged him to welcome Liu Shiche and set him up as emperor; Xu agreed at first, then seized his men and made him his marshal, and once Liu Shiche had been sent to Qi and Qi and had taken every town he approached, Xu had him killed instead. What Xu relied on was calculation and power play rather than any claim of legitimacy. The officers and insiders who mattered as much: Liu Botong, the lieutenant of Jizhou, who seized the governor Dou Wuben and handed Jizhou over to Xu - the earliest insider move in Shandong; Yang Xiaocheng of Jinxiang, who broke away from Xu and surrendered Jinxiang city to the Tang, giving the Tang army its first opening; Zhou Wenju, the defender of Qizhou, captured when the city fell; and Sheng Yanshi, the Tang envoy sent to pacify the people of Henan, who was detained by Xu in the eighth month of the fourth year of Wude (621) and thereby supplied the pretext for revolt. Among the Tang commanders, Prince of Qin Li Shimin was decisive: in the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude he struck at Xu, took more than ten cities, shook the Huai and Si regions and drove Du Fuyei of Huainan to court. Xingtai minbu shangshu Shi Wanbao took Chenzhou, Liangzhou zongguan Wang Yaohan took Qizhou, and Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, xingjun zongguan Ren Gui and Li Shiji continued the advance after the Prince of Qin had swept the Huai-Ji region, until Xu was forced out of his city. Liu Heitao, Li Mi, Dou Jiande and Du Fuyei were the outside figures who decided Xu's fate: the defeat of Liu Heitao left him panicked, Dou Jiande had once sheltered him, and Li Mi was the man he had served under. And the prefectural officers, city defenders and strategists such as Dou Wuben, Yang Xiaocheng, Zhou Wenju, Liu Fuli and Liu Shiche were the joints at which the situation turned again and again.
kits: 本卡所示的埃及月牙劍（Khopesh）是一件青銅時代的單刃彎刀，形制外彎、刃口近柄處內鉤，砍入之後不必把刀拔出來再砍第二下，是古埃及第二王朝中期（約公元前1500年）劍匠的設計，比本場戰爭早了三千一百多年。必須說明的是：這件兵器不可能出現在隋末的魯郡戰場上，山東平原上的兩軍從未見過這種形制的刀。它在此卡上的位置，是作為「近身劈砍兵器」這一功能類別的代表——在同一個功能座標上，617年的中國戰場上真正在用的是鐵刀：隋唐環首刀（時稱橢刀）直刃方頭，柄端設環，騎兵佩於腰間，步兵則以刀配槊、矛使用；此外還有方天畫戟一類長柄戟、槊、矛、蹶張弩與臂弓、角弓，護具則是皮甲、札甲以及帶護心圓盤的明光鎧。攻城方面，車具包括撞車、雲梯、巢車，以及以機發的石砲；隋末唐初的洛陽、懷州戰役已有「發火車」與「霹靂車」的記載，前者以火藥火油焚燒城壘，後者是鐵包覆的撞擊車，可見這一時期的攻城已不只靠人馬硬撞。起義軍一側則完全相反：民間竹木標槊、削尖的竹竿、漁叉與土製弓弩為主，甲胄極少，鎧甲多為繳獲的隋軍舊物，攻城全靠人多而無車具。馬匹方面，兗泗一帶是北方的產馬地，起義眾初期靠徵集與繳獲的散馬維持騎兵規模，唐軍則以關中精騎配馬槊、角弓與馬鎧作機動主力，糧秣沿泗水、濟水、汴水、淮水的水路與車運維持，濟兗一線的糧道是雙方爭奪的重點。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh shown on this card is a single-edged bronze blade with an outward curve and a hook near the hilt, designed so that once it has bitten into a target it does not have to be pulled back out to strike a second time; it belongs to the workshops of the Middle Kingdom of Egypt, around 1500 BC, and is roughly three thousand one hundred years older than this war. It must be said plainly: this weapon cannot have appeared on a battlefield in Lu commandery in the late Sui, and neither army on the Shandong plain ever saw a blade of that form. Its place on the card is as the representative of one functional family, that of the close-quarters chopping weapon. On the very same functional coordinate, what was actually in use on a Chinese battlefield in 617 was the iron sabre: the Sui and Tang ring-pommel sabre, then called a tuodao, had a straight edge and a square tip with a ring at the end of the grip, carried at the waist by cavalry and used by infantry in company with pikes and spears. Alongside it were long-hafted halberds of the fangtian huaji type, long pikes, spears, the crossbow drawn by a foot pedal, and bow arms and horn bows; for protection there were leather armour, lacquered lamellar armour and the mingguang armour with its bright metal breast disc. On the siege side the equipment included battering rams, scaling ladders, observation towers and stone-throwing machines powered by a torsion mechanism. The campaigns at Luoyang and Huaizhou in the last years of the Sui and the early Tang already record the fire wagon and the thunderbolt car, the former burning palisades with gunpowder and burning oil, the latter an iron-shod ramming vehicle, which shows that sieging in this period was no longer a matter of men and horses alone. The rebels were exactly the opposite: bamboo and wooden throwing pikes, sharpened bamboo poles, fish spears and home-made crossbows, with almost no body armour and cuirasses mostly taken from captured Sui equipment, and sieges conducted by sheer numbers without a single siege engine. On horses: the Yanzhou-Sishui region was a northern breeding ground, so the insurgents at first kept a mounted force alive with requisitioned and captured strays, while the Tang relied on Guanzhong elite cavalry equipped with horse pikes, horn bows and barding as their mobile striking force; grain moved along the waterways of the Si, Ji, Bian and Huai rivers and by wagon, which made the supply line through the Ji-Yanzhou corridor the point both sides fought over.
tactics: 起義一方採取的是隋末典型的州郡流動作戰：以魯郡為策源地，先取鄰近縣邑，再沿泗水、濟水向杞、陳、宋城方向擴張；攻城多靠內應開城門（濟州即由別駕劉伯通執刺史竇務本而得），守城則倚靠城垣、糧食與地形作消耗，試圖以持久戰拖垮唐廷在山東的接收。623年正月前的一度反唐，其戰術意圖非常清楚：扣留盛彥師，切斷唐廷在河南的安集鏈路，與在河北起兵的劉黑闔南北呼應，使唐軍必須分兵兩線而不能專注一路。但劉黑闔在洺水（621年）敗北後北走河北，呼應斷絕，徐圓朗隨即陷入被各路唐軍圍剿的處境。唐方的戰術則是典型的隋唐式攻城加掃蕩：以州兵圍城、由行台民部尚書與總管分路奪城，先取杞州（王要漢）、再取陳州（史萬寶），斷其西面與南面的支點；同時用「叛出」與「內應」瓦解徐圓朗的城邑網，金鄉的陽孝誠即為典型，敵我力量的此消彼長先在城邑層面完成。秋七月秦王李世民率精騎投入戰場後，戰術重心由攻城轉為野戰追擊，一役而連下十餘城，聲震淮泗，淮、濟之間的整個據點網被迅速拆散；其後唐廷不再以主力反覆攻堅，而由淮安王李神通、行軍總管任瑰、李世勣分兵掃蕩殘部，切斷糧道、封鎖城邑，等待徐圓朗部眾自潰。與此同時，李建成在河北擊滅劉黑闔，等於抽掉了徐圓朗唯一的外援，使唐軍得以在河北與山東兩個戰場同時收束。
tacticsEn: The insurgents fought in the typical late-Sui fashion of a county-level mobile war: they made Lu commandery their base of operations, took the neighbouring walled towns first, and then spread west and south along the Si and Ji rivers towards Qizhou, Chenzhou and Song city. Cities were taken mainly through insiders opening the gates, as at Jizhou, where the lieutenant Liu Botong seized the governor Dou Wuben and handed the city over; defence relied on walls, grain and terrain in a war of attrition, in the hope of wearing out the Tang court's attempt to take over Shandong. The intent behind the renewed revolt of 621 is clear from the tactics: detaining Sheng Yanshi cut the Tang chain of pacification in Henan, and it was meant to work with Liu Heitao's rising in Hebei so that the Tang army would have to split its forces and could not concentrate on one front. But when Liu Heitao was defeated at Mingshui in 621 and withdrew north into Hebei, the link was broken, and Xu Yuanlang was immediately surrounded by the converging Tang columns. The Tang method was the classic Sui-Tang combination of siege and sweep: prefectural troops ringed the cities while the xingtai minbu shangshu and the zongguan took towns in separate columns, first Qizhou under Wang Yaohan and then Chenzhou under Shi Wanbao, cutting off Xu's footholds to the west and the south; at the same time defections and insider plots pulled apart Xu's network of towns, the case of Yang Xiaocheng of Jinxiang being typical, so that the balance of forces shifted first at the level of individual cities. In the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude the Prince of Qin Li Shimin brought his elite cavalry into the field, and the tactical centre of gravity shifted from siege to pursuit in the open: a single campaign took more than ten cities, shook the Huai and Si regions and rapidly dismantled the whole network of strongholds between the Huai and Ji. Thereafter the court no longer threw its main force at stubborn cities; the Prince of Huai'an Li Shentong, the xingjun zongguan Ren Gui and Li Shiji were sent in separate columns to sweep the remnants, cut the supply lines and seal the towns, waiting for Xu's own men to disintegrate. At the same time Li Jiancheng's destruction of Liu Heitao in Hebei removed the only outside support Xu could have counted on, allowing the Tang to close both theatres, Hebei and Shandong, at the same time.
data: 可考的數字不多，但大體可以拼出一幅輪廓。時間：起事於隋大業十三年（617年）正月，終於唐武德六年（623年）正月，前後約六年；中間有兩次轉折，分別是武德二年（619年）降唐受封與武德四年（621年）八月再度反唐。兵員：徐圓朗起兵時眾至數萬，《資治通鑑》只作「眾數萬」的概記，歷代史家多以為其中有誇大成分，可用的戰兵當在萬餘量級；唐軍方面，擊徐圓朗的主攻兵力由數路合兵構成，其中秦王世民所部為關中精騎，淮、濟、泗之間的州兵則分散在十餘座城縣，每路兵數史無詳錄。戰果：武德四年秋七月，世民一役「下十餘城」，是本役最集中的攻城記錄；同年正月已先後有濟州以內應歸附、金鄉叛出降唐、汴州總管王要漢拔杞州、史萬寶拔陳州。地理距離：魯郡兗州至被圍的宋城（今河南商丘一帶）約三百里，至唐都長安約一千四百餘里，這兩個數字說明唐廷調兵與運糧的縱深，遠大於起義軍能控制的範圍。水道：泗水、濟水、汴水、淮水構成山東與中原之間的漕運骨架，順流而下可達淮南，運兵運糧皆賴此線。季節：武德四年七月正在汛期，兵糧易受河水漲落影響；武德六年正月在最寒之際，圍城日久，糧秣與士氣同為致敗之因。
dataEn: The recorded figures are few, but they allow a rough outline to be drawn. Timing: the rising began in the first month of the thirteenth year of Daye (617) and ended in the first month of the sixth year of Wude (623), about six years in all; two turnings fall inside that span, the submission and investiture of 619 and the renewed revolt in the eighth month of the fourth year of Wude (621). Men: Xu Yuanlang's crowd at the start is recorded as several tens of thousands, but the Zizhi Tongjian gives only the general phrase several tens of thousands, later historians generally treat it as exaggerated, and the effective fighting force was probably in the region of some ten thousand. On the Tang side the main effort against Xu was composed of several columns, the Prince of Qin's being elite cavalry from Guanzhong, while the prefectural troops scattered across the Huai, Ji and Si areas were spread over more than ten walled towns, and no strength figures survive for any single column. Results: in the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude the Prince of Qin took more than ten cities in a single campaign, the most concentrated record of siege work in this war; earlier in the same first month Jizhou had been handed over through an insider, Jinxiang had been surrendered by a defector, Liangzhou zongguan Wang Yaohan had taken Qizhou and Shi Wanbao had taken Chenzhou. Distances: from Yanzhou in Lu commandery to Song city, which was besieged, the modern Shangqiu area, is about three hundred li, and to the Tang capital Chang'an about one thousand four hundred li and more - two numbers that show how much greater the depth for moving troops and grain was than anything the insurgents could control. Waterways: the Si, Ji, Bian and Huai rivers formed the skeleton of transport between Shandong and the central plain, running downstream towards Huainan, and both men and grain moved along that line. Season: the seventh month of the fourth year of Wude fell in the flood season, when troop movements and grain were easily affected by the rivers; the first month of the sixth year of Wude was the coldest season, and a protracted siege brought supply and morale down together to the point of defeat.
cause: 起義的直接背景，是隋朝在大業末年已從中央到地方全面崩解。隋煬帝自大業七年（611年）起三次征伐高句麗，河北山東丁壯的調發與租調的加派，耗盡了地方社會的承受力；到大業十三年（617年），隋廷的政令已不能出京畿。魯郡一帶的賦役與鹽漕之弊是民間積怨的直接來源，泗水、濟水一線是漕運孔道，州縣官吏在此處的徵發與截留，往往把壓力轉嫁給最底層的丁壯。隋末的農民起事自王薄於大業七年首倡之後已連成一片，泰山、魯郡、長清一帶的亡命與逃戶聚集在山澤之間，只等一個契機便成建制。起事者本身的算盤也清楚：起兵不必立刻打出反隋的旗號，先以「聚眾」與「據城」造成既成事實，再在李密、竇建德、唐之間待價而沽。隋室內部的裂痕同樣重要：江都之變（618年）後，楊侑在洛陽被立為帝、宇文化及與裴矩在江都擁立楊侖，隋朝名號分裂，兗州一帶的州兵與豪強不必再顧慮名義上的朝廷。至於徐圓朗本人，其於大業十三年正月在魯郡起兵、隨後依附李密，正是「先據一州、再擇強鄰」這一路線的體現，也解釋了他為什麼在武德二年選擇歸唐、又能在武德四年重新舉起反旗：山東這塊地本身才是他真正的本錢。
causeEn: The immediate background to the rising is that the Sui had collapsed from the centre outwards by the last years of the Daye era. From the seventh year of Daye (611) the Yangdi emperor had waged three campaigns against Goguryeo, and the repeated levies of corvée from the male population of Hebei and Shandong, together with increased taxes, drained what the local society could bear; by the thirteenth year of Daye (617) the Sui court's decrees no longer travelled beyond the capital region. In the Lu commandery the burden of levies and the abuses of the salt and transport system were the direct source of popular grievance: the Si and Ji rivers were the artery of the grain traffic, and the way county officials levied and intercepted along that line consistently shifted the pressure down onto the poorest of the labouring households. The peasant risings that began with Wang Bo in 611 had by now merged into one; the fugitives and runaways who gathered in the hills and marshes around Mount Tai, Lu and Changqing only needed a spark to become an armed force. The calculation behind the revolt was equally clear: it was not necessary to fly an anti-Sui banner at the outset. One could first create fait accompli by gathering a crowd and holding a city, and then sell one's services to the highest bidder among Li Mi, Dou Jiande and the Tang. The fractures inside the Sui house mattered too: after the change of rule at Jiangdu in 618, Yang You was set up as emperor at Luoyang while Yuwen Huaji and Pei Ju enthroned Yang Jian at Jiangdu, so that Sui authority was split in name as well, and the prefectural troops and local strongmen of Yanzhou no longer needed to worry about a nominal court. As for Xu Yuanlang himself, raising men in Lu commandery in the first month of the thirteenth year of Daye and then attaching himself to Li Mi exemplifies the line of first seizing one prefecture and then choosing a strong neighbour; it also explains why he chose to submit to the Tang in the second year of Wude and yet could raise his banner again in the fourth: the territory of Shandong was his real capital.
impact: 徐圓朗起義在隋末唐初的格局中不是一場決定性的戰役，卻是唐廷必須認真對待的一塊拼圖。它延宕了唐對山東的接管：自617年起，兗、泗、杞、陳一線在長達六年的時間裡處於半獨立狀態，唐廷在山東的有效統治直到623年才真正完成；在此期間，河南與河北之間的漕運與兵力調動始終受制於這條斷裂線。其次，它牽制了唐廷對河北的用兵。武德四年徐圓朗與劉黑闔一南一北遙相呼應，使唐廷必須同時在兩個方向上部署兵力，這是劉黑闔得以在河北重建勢力、並在623年迫使唐廷動用齊王李建成再行征伐的重要外部條件之一。第三，它改變了北方群雄的座次：徐圓朗先依李密、後歸竇建德、再降唐、再反唐，這一連串轉換本身就是隋末群雄互相吞併的縮影，兗州、鄆州一帶的豪強與流民在戰亂中被重新洗牌。第四，從軍事技術史看，此役留下了隋唐易代之際山東戰場的典型樣本：州兵與流民武裝如何依托城垣與水道進行持久抵抗，中央朝廷又如何用離間、拔城與精騎掃蕩的組合逐步壓縮他們的活動空間，這些經驗在後來唐初平定江南與收拾河北的過程中被反覆使用。到唐太宗貞觀年間，山東已從戰亂最烈之處轉為漕運與馬政的重要供給區，而這條轉變的起點，正是623年徐圓朗據地悉平的那一年。
impactEn: Xu Yuanlang's rising was not a decisive battle in the shape of the late Sui and early Tang, but it was a piece the Tang court had to take seriously. It delayed the Tang takeover of Shandong: from 617 onward the line of Yanzhou, Si, Qi and Chen remained in a half-independent condition for six full years, and effective Tang rule over the region was not complete until 623; throughout that period the movement of grain and troops between Henan and Hebei was permanently constrained by this fracture. Second, it tied down Tang resources meant for Hebei. In the fourth year of Wude, with Xu Yuanlang and Liu Heitao calling to each other from south and north, the court had to deploy in two directions at once, and that was one of the important external conditions allowing Liu Heitao to rebuild his power in Hebei and forcing the court in 623 to bring in Prince of Qi Li Jiancheng for a fresh campaign. Third, it rearranged the ranking of the northern contenders: Xu Yuanlang's sequence of first serving Li Mi, then going over to Dou Jiande, then surrendering to the Tang, then revolting again is itself a miniature of the mutual absorption of the late Sui, and the strongmen and runaways of Yanzhou and Yun prefecture were reshuffled by the fighting. Fourth, in the military-technical history of the transition, this campaign left a typical sample of a Shandong battlefield at the turn of the dynasties: how prefectural troops and armed runaways could sustain resistance behind walls and waterways, and how a central court, in turn, closed the space around them by combining defection, the reduction of cities and cavalry sweeps - lessons used repeatedly in the early Tang campaigns against Jiangnan and Hebei. By the Zhenguan reign of Emperor Taizong, Shandong had turned from the worst-hit battlefield into an important supply base for transport and for the horse herds, and the starting point of that turn was precisely the year 623, when Xu Yuanlang's strongholds were levelled.
result: 結果可以分三段看。第一段是失敗：李密敗亡後他歸入竇建德，雖未被消滅，卻也沒有得到真正的地盤；只有在唐廷給出官爵與編戶的承認之後，他才從流寇變成受編制的軍人。第二段是反覆：武德二年受封魯郡公、拜兗州總管，看似歸順，卻在武德四年（621年）八月扣留唐使盛彥師，重新起兵反唐，圍攻宋城，與劉黑闔相呼應，結果是孤軍無援——劉黑闔在洺水敗北後北走河北，他隨即失去了唯一可以指望的呼應方。第三段是終局：唐廷以李世民的騎兵在淮濟地區連下十餘城、拆散其據點網絡，再由李神通、任瑰、李世勣分路掃蕩，同時李建成在河北擊滅劉黑闔，雙線合攏；徐圓朗眾盡糧絕，兵敗窮蹙，與數騎棄城出走，終為人所殺，《資治通鑑》記作「與數騎棄城走，為野人所殺」，兗泗一帶「其地悉平」。此役平定之後，唐廷完成了對山東的直接控制，為隨後平定河北、進軍江南掃清了側翼；而徐圓朗這個在六年之間三次改變陣營的山東起事首領，也隨兗州復歸朝廷而退出了歷史舞臺。
resultEn: The outcome can be read in three stages. The first is failure: after Li Mi's collapse Xu Yuanlang went over to Dou Jiande, and although he was not destroyed, he gained no territory of his own; only when the Tang court gave him rank and enrolled him did he change from a roving band leader into a man on the rolls. The second is the reversal: in the second year of Wude he was made Duke of Lu and jiangjun of Yanzhou, which looked like submission, yet in the eighth month of the fourth year of Wude (621) he detained the Tang envoy Sheng Yanshi, rose in revolt once more, besieged Song city and called in concert with Liu Heitao - and found himself isolated without support, for when Liu Heitao was beaten at Mingshui and withdrew north into Hebei, Xu lost the only partner he could have counted on. The third is the end: the court used Li Shimin's cavalry to take more than ten cities in the Huai-Ji region and dismantle the network of strongholds, then sent Li Shentong, Ren Gui and Li Shiji in separate columns to sweep the remnants, while Li Jiancheng destroyed Liu Heitao in Hebei and the two lines closed together. Xu's men ran out of food, the army was beaten and exhausted, and he left the city with a few riders only to be killed; the Zizhi Tongjian records that, cornered and desperate, he abandoned the city with a few horsemen and was killed by those who found him, and that in the lands of Yanzhou and Si everything was thereby levelled. With this campaign settled, the Tang completed their direct control of Shandong and cleared the flank for the subsequent reduction of Hebei and the advance into Jiangnan; and Xu Yuanlang, the Shandong rebel leader who had changed sides three times in six years, left the stage of history as Yanzhou returned to the court.
